hints.content:
###Graphing the equations

The equations are both in *slope intercept form*: $y=\goldD{m}x+\purpleC{b}$. We can use the $y$-intercept and slope to identify points on each line.

The line given by the first equation $y=\goldD{4}x\purpleC{-2}
$ has a $y$-intercept of $(0,\purpleC{-2})$ and a slope of $\goldD{4}$, so another point on that line is $(0+1,\purpleC{-2}\goldD{+4})=(1,2).$ Now we have two points to graph this line.

In a similar manner, we can find that the line given by $y=\goldD{1}x+\purpleC{3}$ passes through $(0,\purpleC{3})$ and $(0+1,\purpleC{3}+\goldD{1})=(1,4)$.

We can graph the lines using these points:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. The equation y equals four x minus two is graphed with the points zero, negative two and one, two plotted on the line. The equation y equals one x plus three is graphed with the points zero, three and one, four plotted on the line.

hints.content:
###Solving the system

When we graph the two lines, we can see that they intersect between $x=1$ and $x=2$ and between $y=4$ and $y=5$:

[[☃ image 1]]

There is only one option that fits this description: $x= 1\dfrac23, y=4\dfrac23$.

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. The equation y equals four x minus two is graphed with the points zero, negative two and one, two plotted on the line. The equation y equals one x plus three is graphed with the points zero, three and one, four plotted on the line. The intersection of these two lines is plotted at an x-value between one and two and a y-value between four and five.
